title: Generalized Leibniz-Type Formulas for Mathematical Constants
description: Formalizes the family of Leibniz-type alternating series that converge to mathematical constants, unified through the Dirichlet beta and eta functions

meta.author: Leibniz (1676), Catalan (1865), Dirichlet
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom: eta-zeta relation η(s) = (1-2^{1-s})ζ(s). 9 sorries for series convergence results requiring analytic tools (alternating series test, Fourier analysis, Abel summation).
originalContributions: Unified framework: Dirichlet beta (β) and eta (η) functions as Leibniz-type series
Definitions of Catalan's constant G = β(2) and Dirichlet character mod 4
Proved algebraic properties: partial sum recurrences, χ₄ periodicity
Complete table of Leibniz-type formulas: β(1)=π/4, β(2)=G, β(3)=π³/32, η(1)=ln2, η(2)=π²/12
Documented irrationality status of each constant

overview.historicalContext: Leibniz discovered $\pi/4 = 1 - 1/3 + 1/5 - \cdots$ in 1676 (though the Kerala school knew equivalent results centuries earlier via Gregory's series). The alternating harmonic series $\ln 2 = 1 - 1/2 + 1/3 - \cdots$ was known to Mercator (1668). Euler systematically evaluated these series in the 1730s-40s, connecting $\beta(3) = \pi^3/32$ to Fourier-type expansions. Dirichlet (1837) revealed the deeper structure: $\beta(s) = L(s, \chi_4)$, a Dirichlet $L$-function for the non-principal character mod 4, whose non-vanishing at $s=1$ proves infinitely many primes $\equiv 1 \pmod{4}$. Catalan introduced $G = \beta(2) \approx 0.9159$ in 1865; its irrationality remains open despite partial results by Zudilin (2001, at least one of $\beta(2)$, $\beta(4)$ is irrational) and Rivoal. The eta-zeta relation $\eta(s) = (1-2^{1-s})\zeta(s)$ was known to Euler and provides the bridge between alternating and non-alternating series.
overview.problemStatement: How do generalized Leibniz-type formulas extend to other constants?
overview.text: The Dirichlet beta and eta functions unify all Leibniz-type alternating series: β(s) = Σ(-1)^n/(2n+1)^s captures π-related constants, while η(s) = Σ(-1)^{n-1}/n^s captures ζ-related constants
overview.proofStrategy: Define the Dirichlet beta and eta functions via partial sums, state convergence results for specific values (s=1,2,3), prove algebraic properties of partial sums, and connect to the underlying L-function structure via the character χ₄.
keyInsights: β(s) captures odd-denominator series (π-related), η(s) captures all-denominator series (ζ-related)
The eta-zeta relation η(s) = (1-2^{1-s})ζ(s) converts between alternating and non-alternating sums
Catalan's constant G = β(2) is perhaps the most important constant whose irrationality is unknown
All these series arise from Dirichlet L-functions: β(s) = L(s,χ₄) for the non-principal character mod 4

All Leibniz-type alternating series arise as evaluations of Dirichlet L-functions: the Leibniz formula gives L(1,χ₄) = π/4 and the alternating harmonic series gives L(1,χ₁) = log 2 via the eta function η(s) = (1-2^{1-s})ζ(s). This L-function perspective unifies seemingly disparate constants through the arithmetic of Dirichlet characters.

sections.title: The Alternating Harmonic Series (ln 2)
sections.summary: Defines the alternating harmonic partial sum and states convergence to $\ln 2$.
sections.mathContext: $\eta(1) = \ln 2$ from the Taylor series of $\ln(1+x)$ at $x = 1$.

sections.title: The Dirichlet Beta Function
sections.summary: Defines the beta partial sum $\beta_n(s) = \sum_{k<n} (-1)^k/(2k+1)^s$ and restates $\beta(1) = \pi/4$.

sections.title: Catalan's Constant
sections.summary: Defines Catalan's constant $G = \beta(2)$, states convergence and positivity.

sections.title: $\beta(3) = \pi^3/32$
sections.summary: States $\beta(3) = \pi^3/32$, requiring Fourier analysis to prove.

sections.title: The Dirichlet Eta Function
sections.summary: Defines the eta partial sum, states $\eta(1) = \ln 2$ and $\eta(2) = \pi^2/12$.

sections.title: The Eta-Zeta Relationship
sections.summary: Axiomatizes $\eta(s) = (1 - 2^{1-s})\zeta(s)$, the sole axiom of the file.

sections.title: The General Leibniz-Type Pattern
sections.summary: Complete table unifying all Leibniz-type formulas via $\beta(s)$ and $\eta(s)$.

sections.title: Proved Algebraic Properties
sections.summary: Proves partial sum recurrences, defines $\chi_4$, proves its periodicity and values.
sections.mathContext: $\chi_4$: the non-principal character mod 4, with $\beta(s) = L(s, \chi_4)$.

sections.title: Irrationality Status and Numerical Bounds
sections.summary: Documents irrationality status of all constants, bounds $0.91 < G < 0.92$, and the Leibniz error bound $|\beta_n(1) - \pi/4| \leq 1/(2n+1)$.
sections.mathContext: All constants transcendental except $G = \beta(2)$ — irrationality unknown.

crossReferences.description: Answers OQ-02: 'How do generalized Leibniz-type formulas extend to other constants?'

conclusion.summary: Leibniz-type alternating series form a unified family through the Dirichlet beta and eta functions. The beta function captures odd-denominator series (yielding π, Catalan's G, π³/32) while the eta function captures all-denominator series (yielding ln 2, π²/12). The underlying structure is L-functions for Dirichlet characters.
conclusion.implications: The framework reveals that Leibniz's π/4 formula is not isolated but is the first member of an infinite family of series converging to important constants. The irrationality of Catalan's constant G = β(2) remains a major open problem.
openQuestions: Can the irrationality of Catalan's constant be proved or disproved?
Can these series convergence results be proved in Lean using Mathlib's analysis infrastructure?
